chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Saad ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Saad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: O Aban! These are the five obligatory prayers. Whoever establishes them and maintains their timings, will meet Allah on the Day of Resurrection, and there is a covenant with Him that will cause Him to enter him into Paradise. And whoever does not pray them for their timings, the matter is left to Him; if He wills, He will forgive him, and if He wills, He will punish him.

key_terms.إِنْ شَاءَ غَفَرَ لَهُ: If He wills, He will forgive him

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for maintaining the timings of the five obligatory prayers according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Thawab al-A'mal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the guaranteed reward for those who maintain the five daily prayers at their precise times and the discretionary fate of those who neglect them. This highlights the Shia emphasis on *muwaqit* (timing) as a critical component of ritual validity, linking consistent observance to a specific divine covenant (*'ahd*) that secures Paradise. The narration underscores the balance between divine promise for diligence and divine mercy or justice for omission, reflecting the juristic focus on both the form and timing of worship.
